title: Random-split rankings poorly predicted microfluidic surrogate rankings under shift
summary: Across 107 held-out groups from six published tables, a random-split ranking of six learned prediction models showed little agreement with their rankings in a simulated adaptive evaluation. Mean Kendall correlation was 0.08, with a reported interval from −0.04 to 0.19.
ai_technology: XGBoost, random and quantile forests, Gaussian processes and neural surrogate models

source_review.scope: Primary §6.4.3 and Table 20, frozen protocols and v1 front matter

evidence.tested: The analysis compared rankings from random-split error with rankings from held-out group performance under the same offline simulated evaluation, using previously published measurements.
evidence.unknown: The comparisons reused finite public tables and modeled lab activity offline. The study did not perform a new laboratory experiment, and the interval does not rule out modest agreement.
evidence.ai_role: Six fitted surrogates made predictions for previously recorded measurements. Comparing their errors under different evaluation procedures quantified how poorly random-split standings carried across the tested settings.
